newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises 70 bps to 12.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises 70 bps to 12.7 pct.

text.p: Croatian average lending rate rose 70 basis points to 12.7 percent on Friday on the high cost of term borrowings despite strong supply, dealers said.
Daily settlements were put at 37 million kuna, against 70 million on offer. Fresh loans accounted for 19.4 million kuna.
The weighted call money rate ended at 9.9 percent after one lender accepted an eight-percent deal.
Interbank term loans were granted at 12 and 15 percent.
Insurers rolled over previous one-week loans at a steady nine percent. Banks renewed two-week and one-month deals at between 15 and 18 percent, and three-month funds at 22 percent.

The central bank calculated its kuna mid-rates for Saturday and next Monday firmer at 6.1297 against the dollar and at 3.5752 against the German mark. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom 385-1-4557075
